nodes.summary: For every $n$-state Busy Beaver machine $M$ and every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, if $h \in \mathbb{Z}$ is the head position after $M$ has run for $t$ steps from the initial configuration on the blank tape, then $|h| \le t$.
nodes.title: Head displacement bound

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $B$, the runtime-bound sentence is the sentence code with tag $3$ and payload $\langle n, B \rangle$, the pairing of $n$ and $B$; as a number it equals $4 \langle n, B \rangle + 3$.
nodes.title: Runtime-bound sentence

nodes.summary: Rado's score function $\Sigma$ satisfies $\Sigma(5) = 4098$: among the two-symbol Busy Beaver machines with $5$ working states that halt when started on the blank tape, the largest number of ones left on the tape at the halting time is $4098$.
nodes.title: Five-state Busy Beaver score value

nodes.summary: Rado's score function $\Sigma$ satisfies $\Sigma(4) = 13$: among the two-symbol Busy Beaver machines with $4$ working states that halt when started on the blank tape, the largest number of ones left on the tape at the halting time is $13$.
nodes.title: Four-state Busy Beaver score value

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, Rado's score function $\Sigma$ and Rado's shift function $S$ satisfy $\Sigma(n) \le S(n)$: the largest number of ones left on the tape by a halting $n$-state two-symbol machine started on the blank tape is at most the largest halting time of such a machine.
nodes.title: The Busy Beaver score is at most the shift

nodes.summary: Rado's score function $\Sigma$ satisfies $\Sigma(3) = 6$: among the two-symbol Busy Beaver machines with $3$ working states that halt when started on the blank tape, the largest number of ones left on the tape at the halting time is $6$.
nodes.title: Three-state Busy Beaver score value

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, Rado's score function $\Sigma(n)$ is the largest number of ones left on the tape, at its halting time, by an $n$-state two-symbol machine that halts when started on the blank tape; machines that do not halt contribute $0$.
nodes.title: Busy Beaver score function

nodes.summary: Rado's shift function $S$ satisfies $S(5) = 47176870$: among the two-symbol Busy Beaver machines with $5$ working states that halt when started on the blank tape, the largest halting time is $47176870$.
nodes.title: Five-state Busy Beaver shift value

nodes.summary: Rado's shift function $S$ satisfies $S(4) = 107$: among the two-symbol Busy Beaver machines with $4$ working states that halt when started on the blank tape, the largest halting time is $107$.
nodes.title: Four-state Busy Beaver shift value

nodes.summary: Rado's shift function $S$ satisfies $S(3) = 21$: among the two-symbol Busy Beaver machines with $3$ working states that halt when started on the blank tape, the largest halting time is $21$.
nodes.title: Three-state Busy Beaver shift value

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, Rado's shift function $S(n)$ is the largest halting time of an $n$-state two-symbol machine that halts when started on the blank tape; machines that do not halt contribute $0$.
nodes.title: Busy Beaver shift function

nodes.summary: A configuration of an $n$-state machine consists of a current state, which is either one of the $n$ working states or the halt state, an integer head position, and a tape assigning a symbol in $\{0, 1\}$ to every integer cell.
nodes.title: Busy Beaver machine configuration

nodes.summary: A formal theory $T$ is consistent when $T$ does not prove the false sentence.
nodes.title: Consistent formal theory

nodes.summary: For every ZFC-like presentation $Z$ and every $n \le 5$, the theory presented by $Z$ decides halting for $n$-state machines: for every $n$-state machine it proves the machine's halting sentence or its non-halting sentence.
nodes.title: ZFC-like theories decide halting through five states

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a formal theory such that, for every $m$ and every Busy Beaver machine $M$ with $m$ working states, if $T$ proves the halting sentence of the embedding of $M$ into $m + 1$ states then $T$ proves the halting sentence of $M$, and if $T$ proves the non-halting sentence of the embedding of $M$ into $m + 1$ states then $T$ proves the non-halting sentence of $M$. Then for every $n$, if $T$ decides halting for…
nodes.title: Decidability of halting passes to fewer states

nodes.summary: A formal theory $T$ decides halting for $n$-state machines when, for every $n$-state machine $M$, $T$ proves the halting sentence of $M$ or $T$ proves the non-halting sentence of $M$.
nodes.title: Theories deciding halting at a state count

nodes.summary: For a configuration $c$ of an $n$-state machine, its embedding is the configuration for $n + 1$ states with the same head position and the same tape as $c$. Its state is the state of $c$, where a working state $q \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ stays $q$ and the halt state stays the halt state.
nodes.title: Embedding a configuration into one more state

nodes.summary: An $n$-state machine $M$ is embedded into $n + 1$ states as follows. In a working state $q < n$ reading a symbol $s$, the new machine writes the symbol, makes the move and enters the next state that $M$ prescribes in state $q$ on $s$, halting when $M$ halts. In the new state $n$ it writes $0$, moves left and halts, whatever it reads.
nodes.title: Embedding a machine into one more state

nodes.summary: Let $\Sigma(n)$ be the busy beaver score function, the largest score of an $n$-state machine, where the score of a machine is the number of ones on its final tape if it halts on the blank tape and $0$ otherwise. For every $n$, some $n$-state machine $M$ has score equal to $\Sigma(n)$. Thus $\Sigma(n)$ is the number of ones left by a halting $n$-state machine, or $\Sigma(n) = 0$.
nodes.title: The score function is attained

nodes.summary: Let $S(n)$ be Rado's shift function, the largest runtime of an $n$-state machine, where the runtime of a machine is its halting time on the blank tape if it halts and $0$ otherwise. For every $n$, some $n$-state machine $M$ has runtime equal to $S(n)$. Thus $S(n)$ is the halting time of a halting $n$-state machine, or $S(n) = 0$.
nodes.title: The shift function is attained

nodes.summary: The false sentence is the sentence code with tag $2$ and payload $0$, that is, the natural number $2$.
nodes.title: The false sentence

nodes.summary: For a formal theory $T$, the first undecidable number of states is the least $n$ such that $T$ does not decide halting for all $n$-state machines, that is, there is an $n$-state machine $M$ for which $T$ proves neither the halting sentence nor the non-halting sentence of $M$. It is $0$ when there is no such $n$.
nodes.title: First undecidable number of states

nodes.summary: A formal theory is given by a provability predicate on sentence codes, which are natural numbers: for each natural number it specifies whether that sentence code is provable in the theory.
nodes.title: Formal theory

nodes.summary: For an $n$-state machine $M$ that halts on the blank tape, its halting time is the least $t$ such that $M$, started on the blank tape, is in the halt state after $t$ steps.
nodes.title: Halting time

nodes.summary: For an $n$-state machine $M$, the halting sentence of $M$ is the sentence code with tag $0$ and payload the code of $M$. It stands for "$M$ halts on the blank tape"; this meaning comes from soundness hypotheses on a theory, not from the code itself.
nodes.title: Halting sentence of a machine

nodes.summary: Every halting one-state machine halts within one step.
nodes.title: One-state machines halt within one step

nodes.summary: A Busy Beaver machine $M$ with $n$ working states halts within $t$ steps when the configuration reached after running $M$ for $t$ steps from the initial blank-tape configuration is in the halt state.
nodes.title: Halting within $t$ steps

nodes.summary: A Busy Beaver machine $M$ halts when there is a number of steps $t$ such that $M$ halts within $t$ steps, that is, when $M$ started from the initial blank-tape configuration eventually reaches the halt state.
nodes.title: Halting on the blank tape

nodes.summary: For a machine with $n$ working states, the initial state is state $0$ when $n > 0$, and the halt state when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Initial state

nodes.summary: The initial configuration of a machine with $n$ working states is in the initial state (state $0$, or the halt state when $n = 0$), with the head at position $0$ and every tape cell blank, that is, holding the symbol $0$.
nodes.title: Initial configuration of a Busy Beaver machine

nodes.summary: The code of a machine $M$ with $n$ working states is the natural number that encodes the pair $(n, i)$ under a fixed pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, where $i$ is the index of $M$ in a fixed enumeration of the finitely many machines with $n$ working states.
nodes.title: Machine code

nodes.summary: A Busy Beaver machine with $n$ working states is a transition table that assigns to each of the $n$ working states and each read symbol in $\{0, 1\}$ a symbol in $\{0, 1\}$ to write, a head movement (left or right), and a next state, which is either one of the $n$ working states or the halt state.
nodes.title: Busy Beaver machine

nodes.summary: For every Busy Beaver machine $M$, every $t \in \mathbb{N}$ and every cell $i \in \mathbb{Z}$, if cell $i$ holds the symbol $1$ after $M$ runs for $t$ steps from the initial blank-tape configuration, then $-t \le i \le t$.
nodes.title: After $t$ steps, every one lies within distance $t$ of the origin

nodes.summary: A head movement is one of exactly two directions: left or right.
nodes.title: Head movement

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a formal theory and $M$ a Busy Beaver machine with $n$ working states. Suppose that $M$ halts if and only if $T$ proves the false sentence, that $M$ halts whenever $T$ proves the halting sentence of $M$, that $T$ is consistent, and that $T$ does not prove the non-halting sentence of $M$. Then $T$ does not decide halting for all machines with $n$ working states.
nodes.title: A consistency-search machine blocks decidability at its size

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Busy Beaver machine with a single working state $0$. If the transition of $M$ from state $0$ on reading the blank symbol $0$ has next state $0$, then $M$ does not halt.
nodes.title: A one-state machine that stays in its state on a blank never halts

nodes.summary: For a Busy Beaver machine $M$, the non-halting sentence of $M$ is the sentence code with tag $1$ whose payload is the code of $M$; it stands for "$M$ does not halt on the blank tape".
nodes.title: Non-halting sentence of a machine

nodes.summary: For every Busy Beaver machine $M$ and every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of ones of $M$ after $t$ steps is at most $t$.
nodes.title: At most $t$ ones after $t$ steps

nodes.summary: For every Busy Beaver machine $M$ and every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of ones of $M$ after $t + 1$ steps is at most the number of ones of $M$ after $t$ steps plus $1$.
nodes.title: The number of ones grows by at most one per step

nodes.summary: For a Busy Beaver machine $M$ and $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the number of ones of $M$ after $t$ steps is the number of cells $i \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $-t \le i \le t$ that hold the symbol $1$ in the configuration of $M$ after $t$ steps, started on the blank tape.
nodes.title: Number of ones after $t$ steps

nodes.summary: For a Busy Beaver machine $M$ and $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the configuration of $M$ after $t$ steps is the result of applying the one-step map of $M$ $t$ times to the initial configuration on the blank tape.
nodes.title: Configuration after $t$ steps

nodes.summary: For a Busy Beaver machine $M$: if $M$ halts on the blank tape, with halting time $T$, its score is the number of ones of $M$ after $T$ steps; if $M$ does not halt, its score is $0$.
nodes.title: Score of a machine

nodes.summary: The sentence code with tag $a$ and payload $p$ is the natural number $4p + a$. The tags in use are $0$ (the coded machine halts), $1$ (the coded machine does not halt), $2$ (the false sentence), and $3$ with payload the pairing code of $n$ and $B$ (every halting $n$-state machine halts within $B$ steps).
nodes.title: Sentence codes

nodes.summary: The displacement of a head movement is $-1$ for a move to the left and $1$ for a move to the right.
nodes.title: Head displacement

nodes.summary: If a formal theory $T$ decides halting for $n$-state machines for every $n \le 5$, and fails to decide halting for $n$-state machines for some $n$, then the first undecidable size of $T$ is at least $6$.
nodes.title: Decidability through five states and the first undecidable size

nodes.summary: A formal theory $T$ is sound for halting sentences when, for every $n$ and every Busy Beaver machine $M$ with $n$ states, if $T$ proves the halting sentence of $M$ then $M$ halts on the blank tape, and if $T$ proves the non-halting sentence of $M$ then $M$ does not halt on the blank tape.
nodes.title: Soundness for halting sentences

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a machine with $n$ working states and let $c$ be a configuration with head position $h$. If $c$ is halted, the step leaves $c$ unchanged. Otherwise let $q$ be the current state, let $a$ be the symbol in cell $h$, and let $M(q, a) = (b, d, q')$. The step writes $b$ in cell $h$, leaving every other cell unchanged, moves the head to $h - 1$ if $d$ is left and to $h + 1$ if $d$ is right, and passes to the…
nodes.title: One step of a Busy Beaver machine

nodes.summary: For a machine $M$ with $n$ working states, the runtime of $M$ is its halting time on the blank tape if $M$ halts, and $0$ if $M$ does not halt. This is the quantity whose maximum over all $n$-state machines is the shift function $S(n)$.
nodes.title: Runtime of a Busy Beaver machine

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a machine with $n$ working states, started in cell $0$ on the blank tape. For every $t \in \mathbb{N}$ and every cell $i \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $|i| > t$, the symbol in cell $i$ after $t$ steps is $0$.
nodes.title: Cells far from the origin stay blank

nodes.summary: A ZFC-like presentation consists of a formal theory $T$, given by a provability predicate on sentence codes in $\mathbb{N}$, together with a Boolean proof checker $\mathrm{check}(p, s)$ on pairs of natural numbers, such that the following hold. A sentence code $s$ is provable in $T$ if and only if $\mathrm{check}(p, s)$ is true for some $p \in \mathbb{N}$. $T$ is sound for halting: for every machine $M$, if $T$…
nodes.title: Proof-checker presentation of a ZFC-like theory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
